title: From Writing Advice to Manuscript Governance: A Constrained-Transformation Framework for Academic Revision
abstract: arXiv:2610.33001v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Academic revision presents a governance problem when legitimate writing objectives conflict. Writing-process and social-science research show that revision is recursive and that wording carries epistemic and disciplinary commitments. Those literatures identify important constraints but do not settle which objective should prevail when concision, outlet form or stylistic variation conflicts with evidence and claim boundaries. This paper models revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints. Task-relative invariants, contextual constraints and mutable presentation choices define the admissible space; a claim-preservation contract links evidence and judgement to an authorised claim boundary. Four governance propositions specify preservation, precedence, context and sufficiency. translated_title: 从写作建议到稿件治理：一个面向学术修订的受约束转换框架
translated_abstract: 当正当的写作目标之间发生冲突时，学术修订便构成了一个治理问题。写作过程与社会科学领域的研究表明，修订是递归式的，且措辞承载着认识论与学科层面的承诺。这些文献指出了重要的约束条件，但并未解决当简洁性、发表载体形式或风格变化与证据及论断边界发生冲突时，应当以哪个目标优先的问题。本文将修订建模为有序约束下的可容许性问题：任务相关的不可变量、情境约束与可变的表述选择共同界定了可容许空间；一项论断保留契约将证据与判断连接至一个经授权的论断边界。四条治理命题分别规定了保留、优先级、情境与充分性。学术写作过滤器通过筛选候选修订来实现该模型；它并非对优秀学术写作的通用定义或分类器。
tldr: 该论文将学术修订建模为有序约束下的可容许性问题，通过论断保留契约与四条治理命题界定修订的合法边界，并以“学术写作过滤器”对候选修订进行筛选。
en_tdlr: This paper models academic revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints, defining the lawful revision space through a claim-preservation contract and four governance propositions, and implements it as an Academic Writing Filter that screens candidate revisions.
